_note: Not a correspondence table: a list of rival SCHEMES. The tradition does not agree on a letter's temperament, and the play is finding out which scheme is operative in a given puzzle. Each scheme carries the kind of ground it rests on. Generated by build_letters.py; do not hand-edit.

grounding_kinds.PORTAL: An entry in portal/db/turka.db supplies the fact.
grounding_kinds.CORPUS: A Melvin-Koushki paper in research/library supplies it, with a page.
grounding_kinds.REPORTED: PUZZLERIDEAS.txt reports it from a source NOT in this repo. Unverified here.
grounding_kinds.INTERPRETATION: Ours. A design reading, labelled as such wherever it is shown.

reported_but_absent.claim: Ibn ʿArabī assigns hot/cold and dry/moist qualities to groups of letters, alif being responsive to its surroundings.
reported_but_absent.source: PUZZLERIDEAS.txt §7, citing an Oxford study of Ottoman occultism
reported_but_absent.status: The actual assignment is not in this repo. When it is, add it as a fourth temperament scheme; until then no scheme here claims to be his.

reported_but_absent.claim: Kâtib Çelebi reports a division of the letters into four groups by their ṭabāʾiʿ (natures), connected with taksīr.
Two rival explanations of letter efficacy circulate: the mixture of letters, and numerical proportionality between their values.
reported_but_absent.status: Used as the frame for the two 'efficacy' schemes below.

schemes.name: The cycle
schemes.source: The common four-element cycle in abjad order (fire, air, water, earth, repeating). The repo corpus does not give this table; it is included as the most conventional candidate.

schemes.name: By form
schemes.source: Ours: vertical = hot, horizontal = cold, mixed by odd/even dots; closed = moist, open = dry. Built only from the observable form facts in letters.json.

schemes.name: By light
schemes.source: portal entry `ilm-al-huruf`: the 14 light / 14 dark split is sourced. Reading light as hot, dark as cold, and a descending tail as moist, is INTERPRETATION.

schemes.name: Mixture
schemes.source: PUZZLERIDEAS.txt §10: letters act by their combination. Rule here: two neighbours are stable when their temperaments are complementary (fire–air, water–earth share a quality; fire–water and air–earth oppose).

schemes.name: Proportion
schemes.source: PUZZLERIDEAS.txt §10: letters act by numerical proportionality. Rule here: two neighbours are stable when the ratio of their abjad values reduces to small integers (both terms ≤ 4 — the Pythagorean consonances, per portal entry `pythagorean-cosmology`).

schemes.name: Alif is singular
schemes.source: portal entry `abjad-numerology` (alif = 1) and `ilm-al-huruf` (alif as avatar of Oneness). Reading: the only block that may stand on end; it takes no alif on it — two alifs make a line, not two.
